passage:
A small cultural center offered a class in a local language that few young people could speak. At first, only five students joined.
The teacher did not begin with grammar. She began with songs, greetings, family words, and names of foods. She said language is not only for tests. It carries ways of seeing life.
One student asked why they should learn a language that most people no longer used.
The teacher answered, "Because when a language disappears, some jokes, songs, and memories become harder to reach."
By the end of the course, the students could not speak perfectly. But they could greet their grandparents in words that had almost fallen silent.
